explanation.concept: AWS secures 'of' the cloud infrastructure; the customer configures 'in' the cloud
explanation.correct: AWS owns and manages the physical network infrastructure - routers, cabling, and the global backbone connecting Regions and Availability Zones. That's part of security and operations 'of' the cloud, which is entirely AWS's job.

distractors.A: Configuring a VPC's subnets, route tables, and security groups is a customer task - the customer decides how their own network is laid out inside AWS's infrastructure.
distractors.B: Application code is written and maintained by the customer; AWS has no visibility into it.
distractors.C: Monitoring and maintaining application traffic patterns is an operational task that belongs to whoever owns the application - the customer.

explanation.concept: Estimating a not-yet-built project vs. analyzing an already-running account
explanation.correct: Per the stored key, AWS Cost Explorer API is the answer - it lets you pull cost and usage data programmatically and build forecasts you can apply to planning work.

distractors.A: The AWS TCO Calculator compares the cost of an existing on-premises deployment against running the same workload on AWS - it's for migration business cases, not estimating a brand-new project's cost.
distractors.B: AWS Simple Monthly Calculator (the predecessor to today's AWS Pricing Calculator) is the tool actually designed to estimate the cost of a new architecture before it's built, by letting you input hypothetical resource configurations with no dependency on historical usage.
distractors.D: AWS Budgets tracks spending against thresholds you set and alerts you when you're close to or over them - it manages an existing budget, it doesn't estimate a new project's cost from scratch.

5fa8463770c4.needsReview: KEY is C (Cost Explorer API), but Cost Explorer analyzes historical cost/usage data for resources already running - it can't estimate the cost of a project with no usage history yet. The tool actually built for that is the AWS Simple Monthly Calculator / Pricing Calculator (option B).

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor's automated checks span cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor runs automated checks against your account, including a security check that flags security groups with unrestricted (0.0.0.0/0) access to a small set of high-risk ports.

distractors.A: AWS Organizations manages multi-account structure, consolidated billing, and SCPs - it doesn't inspect individual security group rules.
distractors.C: There is no single 'AWS Usage Report' service that audits security group rules; usage reports track billing and consumption metrics.
distractors.D: The EC2 dashboard lets you view and edit security groups manually, but it doesn't proactively scan and flag risky open ports the way Trusted Advisor does.

explanation.concept: Billing alarms live in CloudWatch, on the EstimatedCharges metric
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudWatch can alarm on the AWS-published EstimatedCharges metric (once billing alerts are enabled), notifying you when projected monthly spend crosses a threshold.

distractors.A: AWS Config tracks configuration changes and compliance of resources - it has nothing to do with billing amounts.
distractors.C: AWS X-Ray traces requests through distributed applications for debugging and performance analysis - unrelated to cost.
distractors.D: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity for auditing - it does not track spending or trigger cost alerts.

explanation.concept: Discount scales with commitment length and upfront payment
explanation.correct: All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term combine the longest commitment with full prepayment, which AWS discounts the most heavily compared to On-Demand.

distractors.A: Partial Upfront for a 1-year term combines a shorter commitment and partial prepayment, so the discount is smaller than the 3-year All Upfront option.
distractors.B: All Upfront for a 1-year term prepays in full but for a shorter commitment, earning less discount than the 3-year equivalent.
distractors.D: No Upfront for a 3-year term commits to the term but requires no prepayment, which earns the smallest discount among the RI payment options.

explanation.concept: Physical media destruction is a data-center-level task only AWS can perform
explanation.correct: AWS controls the physical hardware, so decommissioning and physically destroying storage media at end of life is exclusively AWS's responsibility - customers never have physical access to the hardware.

distractors.A: Creating IAM users and groups is entirely the customer's job - AWS has no visibility into how a customer structures their account's identities.
distractors.C: Patching the guest OS on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility, since the customer controls the OS layer under the IaaS model.
distractors.D: Security group configuration is a customer task - it's part of 'security in the cloud.'

explanation.concept: One of AWS's six advantages: stop guessing capacity
explanation.correct: With the cloud, you can scale resources up or down as needed instead of provisioning for a peak demand you predicted months in advance - this removes the need to guess capacity requirements.

distractors.A: AWS does not audit a customer's data; auditing and compliance of customer data is the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.
distractors.B: Data is not 'automatically' secure - customers must configure encryption, access controls, and other security-in-the-cloud measures.
distractors.D: AWS provides compliance-enabling services and reports (e.g., via AWS Artifact), but managing compliance obligations remains the customer's job.

explanation.concept: CloudFront caches content at edge locations for low-latency delivery
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's CDN - it caches a static site's content at edge locations around the world, so visitors are served from a nearby location with lower latency and higher transfer speeds.

distractors.A: AWS Lambda runs backend code on demand - it doesn't cache or accelerate content delivery.
distractors.B: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache for DynamoDB queries - unrelated to serving static website content.
distractors.C: Route 53 is DNS - it resolves domain names to IP addresses but doesn't cache or speed up content transfer.

explanation.concept: Beanstalk automates app deployment; CloudFormation automates infrastructure provisioning
explanation.correct: AWS Elastic Beanstalk automatically handles deploying and scaling web applications, and AWS CloudFormation automates provisioning of the underlying infrastructure from templates - together they cover automated deployment and management on AWS.

distractors.B: AWS CodeCommit is a managed Git repository for storing source code - it doesn't deploy or provision resources itself.
distractors.C: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data movement and transformation between data stores - it's not an application deployment tool.
distractors.E: AWS Config tracks and audits resource configuration state - it doesn't deploy applications.

explanation.concept: Reliability pillar: automated recovery and Multi-AZ redundancy
explanation.correct: The Reliability pillar of the Well-Architected Framework centers on designing for automated recovery from failure and spreading resources across multiple Availability Zones so a single AZ outage doesn't take down the workload.

distractors.C: Managing change through documented processes falls under operational excellence, not reliability design.
distractors.D: Testing for only 'moderate' demand undersells reliability - well-architected systems are tested against peak and failure scenarios, not just typical load.
distractors.E: Backing up recovery to on-premises works against the cloud-native reliability model, which relies on multiple AWS Availability Zones or Regions rather than a return to on-prem infrastructure.

explanation.concept: Contain the breach and get AWS's help - don't destroy evidence
explanation.correct: AWS recommends rotating any potentially exposed passwords and access keys immediately, and contacting AWS Support, who can help assess and remediate the compromise.

distractors.B: Removing MFA tokens weakens your account's security right when you need it most - MFA should be added or enforced, not removed.
distractors.C: Moving resources to a different Region doesn't address compromised credentials, which remain valid account-wide.
distractors.D: Deleting CloudTrail resources destroys the audit trail investigators need - the opposite of what should be done.

explanation.concept: High availability means staying up through failure, not just being reachable
explanation.correct: High availability means an application keeps running for end users even when an underlying resource fails - achieved through redundancy (e.g., multiple Availability Zones) rather than eliminating failures outright.

distractors.A: 24/7 access to AWS technical support is a support-plan benefit, not a property of application availability.
distractors.C: On-demand access to any AWS service describes AWS's consumption pricing model, not high availability.
distractors.D: The ability to deploy anywhere globally is about AWS's global infrastructure and Regions, not about an application surviving a resource failure.

explanation.concept: CloudWatch is AWS's native metrics and monitoring service
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudWatch collects and displays metrics like EC2 CPU utilization, letting the company monitor resource usage and set alarms on it.

distractors.A: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls for auditing - it doesn't collect performance metrics like CPU usage.
distractors.C: The Cost and Usage report details billing and usage data, not real-time performance metrics.
distractors.D: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service - it delivers messages but doesn't itself monitor CPU usage.

explanation.concept: A role is a set of permissions, not an identity with permanent credentials
explanation.correct: An IAM role is an identity with a defined set of permissions that can be assumed temporarily by a user, application, or AWS service - it has no long-term credentials of its own.

distractors.A: A user is a persistent identity with its own long-term credentials, distinct from a role.
distractors.B: A group is a collection of IAM users sharing permissions - not the same construct as a role.
distractors.D: An MFA token is a physical or virtual device used for authentication - unrelated to what a role is.

explanation.concept: RIs trade commitment for discount and capacity reservation
explanation.correct: Reserved Instances give a significant discount over On-Demand pricing in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment, and they let you reserve compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone for guaranteed availability.

distractors.B: RIs don't grant access to additional instance types - you reserve a specific instance family and size you already have access to.
distractors.C: RIs don't add networking capability - they're a billing and capacity construct, not a networking feature.
distractors.D: You can't freely upgrade a standard RI to newer instance types as they release; RIs are tied to the attributes you purchased (Convertible RIs are the exception, not the general rule).

explanation.concept: On-Demand Linux instances bill per second, with a 60-second minimum
explanation.correct: Since AWS moved to per-second billing for On-Demand Linux instances, the customer is billed for the exact 3 hours, 5 minutes, and 6 seconds used - no rounding up to the next minute or hour.

distractors.A: Billing doesn't drop the trailing seconds - per-second billing charges for the full duration, including the 6 seconds.
distractors.C: Rounding to the nearest minute describes the old per-hour billing behavior, not current per-second billing.
distractors.D: Rounding up to the next full hour was the original EC2 billing model, replaced by per-second billing in 2017.

explanation.concept: Compute means running code or containers, not storage or orchestration tooling
explanation.correct: AWS Lambda runs code without provisioning servers, and Amazon ECS runs and orchestrates Docker containers - both are compute services that execute workloads.

distractors.C: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployment to existing compute - it doesn't provide compute capacity itself.
distractors.D: Amazon Glacier (S3 Glacier) is long-term archival storage, not compute.
distractors.E: AWS Organizations manages multi-account governance and billing - it provides no compute capacity.

explanation.concept: CloudFormation turns templates into provisioned infrastructure
explanation.correct: AWS CloudFormation lets you describe your desired infrastructure in a template (JSON or YAML) and automatically provisions and configures the resources it defines - the core of infrastructure as code on AWS.

distractors.A: Amazon GameLift is a managed service for hosting dedicated game servers - unrelated to infrastructure provisioning.
distractors.C: AWS Data Pipeline automates moving and transforming data between services - it doesn't provision general infrastructure.
distractors.D: AWS Glue is a managed ETL service for preparing and cataloging data - not an infrastructure-as-code tool.

explanation.concept: Hybrid architecture needs both a network link and a storage bridge
explanation.correct: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link from on-premises into AWS, and AWS Storage Gateway bridges on-premises applications to AWS storage - together they're standard building blocks for extending an on-prem architecture into the cloud.

distractors.A: Amazon EBS is block storage attached to EC2 instances within AWS - it doesn't connect to or extend an on-premises environment.
distractors.C: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network for distributing content to end users - not a hybrid connectivity tool.
distractors.E: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service - unrelated to extending on-premises infrastructure.

explanation.concept: Direct Connect is a dedicated physical network link, not a VPN over the internet
explanation.correct: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network connection between a customer's data center and AWS, bypassing the public internet entirely.

distractors.A: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for cryptographic key management - it's not a network connectivity service.
distractors.C: AWS VPN connects over the public internet using IPsec tunnels - it's not a dedicated physical connection like Direct Connect.
distractors.D: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center and telephony service, unrelated to network connectivity to AWS.

explanation.concept: Edge locations serve content and absorb attacks close to the end user
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront caches and serves content from edge locations worldwide, and AWS Shield protects applications by absorbing DDoS traffic at those same edge locations.

distractors.C: Amazon EC2 instances run in Availability Zones within a Region, not at edge locations.
distractors.D: Amazon RDS runs in a Region's Availability Zones; it has no presence at edge locations.
distractors.E: Amazon ElastiCache runs within a VPC in a Region - it doesn't operate from edge locations.

explanation.concept: A VPC is the AWS-side network that a hybrid connection terminates into
explanation.correct: Amazon VPC is the customer's private network within AWS, and it's the component a hybrid connection lands in - whether over a VPN or Direct Connect - making it the service that provides network connectivity for a hybrid architecture.

distractors.B: Direct Connect provides the physical link into AWS, but that connectivity is provisioned into and terminates at a VPC, which is what actually joins the on-premises and AWS networks.
distractors.C: AWS Directory Service provides managed directory services (e.g., Active Directory integration) - it's an identity service, not a network connectivity one.
distractors.D: Amazon API Gateway exposes APIs to clients - it doesn't provide the network-level connectivity between on-premises and AWS.

explanation.concept: The TCO Calculator compares on-prem cost against AWS cost, side by side
explanation.correct: The AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator is purpose-built to compare the cost of running a workload in a traditional on-premises environment against running the equivalent workload on AWS.

distractors.A: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes AWS costs you're already incurring - it doesn't compare against a traditional on-premises environment.
distractors.B: AWS Budgets tracks and alerts on spending against thresholds you set - it doesn't perform on-prem-versus-cloud cost comparisons.
distractors.C: The Cost and Usage report itemizes AWS usage and cost - it has no data about, or comparison against, on-premises costs.

explanation.concept: Marketplace bundles licensing into consumption billing and one-click launch
explanation.correct: AWS Marketplace lets customers pay for third-party software on a pay-as-you-go basis bundled into their AWS bill, and its 1-Click deployment launches pre-configured software instantly - both faster and simpler than buying, installing, and licensing software manually on EC2.

distractors.C: Encryption of data is governed by the shared responsibility model based on the underlying AWS service, not by a Marketplace vendor managing it independently.
distractors.D: Marketplace doesn't eliminate the need to upgrade software - customers still manage updates for the software they run, just like self-installed software.
distractors.E: Deploying without testing is never a benefit AWS promotes - proper testing is still expected regardless of the software's source.

explanation.concept: The customer owns everything above the hypervisor: OS, data, and configuration
explanation.correct: Patching guest operating systems and configuring security groups both happen inside the customer's own instances and network - squarely 'security in the cloud,' the customer's half of the shared responsibility model.

distractors.A: Firmware upgrades to network infrastructure are physical, hardware-level tasks that only AWS can perform.
distractors.C: Patching the underlying hypervisor is part of the virtualization layer AWS manages, not something customers can access.
distractors.D: Physical security of AWS data centers is entirely AWS's responsibility - customers have no physical access.

explanation.concept: AWS Config tracks configuration history and evaluates compliance over time
explanation.correct: AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and their changes over time, and evaluates them against rules - giving customers an audit trail and compliance view of how resources have changed.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor gives point-in-time best-practice recommendations - it doesn't record a historical configuration change log.
distractors.B: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service analyzing logs for malicious activity - it doesn't track configuration change history.
distractors.C: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities - it doesn't audit configuration change history.

explanation.concept: CloudFront is AWS's global content delivery network
explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's content delivery network, distributing data, video, and applications to users worldwide from edge locations with low latency and high transfer speeds.

distractors.A: AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure from templates - it has nothing to do with content delivery.
distractors.B: AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated network link to AWS - it doesn't deliver content globally to end users.
distractors.D: Amazon Pinpoint is a marketing and customer-engagement messaging service (email, SMS, push) - unrelated to content delivery.

explanation.concept: Elasticity: capacity flexes automatically with demand
explanation.correct: Elasticity is the ability to automatically scale compute resources up or down to match changing workload demand, avoiding both over-provisioning and under-provisioning.

distractors.A: Security concerns protecting resources from threats, not matching capacity to demand.
distractors.B: Reliability is about a workload consistently performing its intended function, including recovering from failure - not specifically about scaling.
distractors.D: High availability is about minimizing downtime through redundancy, a related but distinct concept from scaling capacity to demand.

explanation.concept: Report abuse of AWS-owned IPs to the AWS Abuse team, not general support
explanation.correct: AWS operates a dedicated Abuse team for reporting misuse of AWS resources, including DDoS activity originating from AWS-owned IP addresses - that's the first point of contact for this kind of report.

distractors.A: AWS Premium (technical) Support handles operational and technical issues with your own resources, not abuse reports about traffic from AWS IPs.
distractors.B: A Technical Account Manager is a named contact for Enterprise Support customers on general account and technical guidance, not the dedicated abuse-reporting channel.
distractors.C: An AWS Solutions Architect advises on architecture design - not the right contact for reporting abusive traffic.

explanation.concept: Cloud economics: no upfront commitment, provision on demand
explanation.correct: Hosting on AWS means no upfront capital commitment and the ability to provision exactly the resources needed, when needed - the pay-as-you-go, on-demand model central to cloud economics.

distractors.B: AWS manages security 'of' the cloud, but the shared responsibility model still leaves the customer responsible for security 'in' the cloud - AWS doesn't manage 'all' security.
distractors.D: Storage is not free or unlimited - customers pay for the storage they consume.
distractors.E: Customers never have control over the physical infrastructure - that stays entirely with AWS.

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor is an automated tool, not a human advisor
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor is an online tool that runs automated checks against your account and reports recommendations across cost optimization, performance, security, and other categories - not a person or partner network.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor is not a staff member - it's an automated, tool-based service.
distractors.B: It's not a network of partners; it's a single AWS-built automated checking service.
distractors.D: Trusted Advisor is a distinct tool from Technical Account Managers, who are human points of contact available under specific support plans.

explanation.concept: Cost Explorer is the visualization and analysis tool for historical and forecasted cost
explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive interface to visualize, understand, and analyze AWS costs and usage over time, including custom reports and forecasts.

distractors.A: AWS Budgets sets spending thresholds and sends alerts - it's for tracking against a budget, not general cost visualization and analysis.
distractors.C: AWS Organizations manages multi-account structure and policies - it doesn't provide cost visualization tooling itself.
distractors.D: Consolidated billing merges multiple accounts' invoices into one bill - it doesn't provide the interactive analysis Cost Explorer does.

explanation.concept: Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS's compliance documentation
explanation.correct: AWS Artifact provides on-demand, self-service access to AWS's compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO, etc.) and agreements, letting customers download the documentation they need for their own audits.

distractors.A: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity within your own account - it doesn't provide AWS's compliance reports.
distractors.C: AWS Health provides alerts and guidance about events affecting your AWS resources - it's not a compliance-report repository.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs - unrelated to compliance documentation.

explanation.concept: Deploy near customers, and let CloudFront's edge network handle the rest
explanation.correct: Companies can deploy in multiple AWS Regions close to their customers to cut latency, and CloudFront's global network of edge locations caches content near users worldwide to further reduce latency.

distractors.B: Amazon Translate translates text and documents on request - it doesn't automatically translate third-party website interfaces.
distractors.D: Amazon Comprehend performs natural language processing (sentiment, entity extraction) - it doesn't build multi-language response applications by itself.
distractors.E: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic within a Region across targets - it does not distribute traffic across multiple Regions.

explanation.concept: Beanstalk takes the uploaded code and handles the deployment plumbing
explanation.correct: AWS Elastic Beanstalk automatically handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, Auto Scaling, and application health monitoring for the application you deploy - you just supply the code.

distractors.A: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration - it doesn't provision capacity or manage deployments.
distractors.C: Amazon Route 53 is DNS and domain routing - it doesn't provision compute capacity or monitor app health.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN for content delivery - it doesn't manage deployment, scaling, or health monitoring of an application.

explanation.concept: Network ACLs are a VPC-level, stateless firewall at the subnet boundary
explanation.correct: Amazon VPC provides network ACLs, which act as a stateless firewall controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level, hardening external connectivity to EC2 instances.

distractors.A: AWS IAM manages identities and permissions for accessing AWS resources and APIs - it doesn't filter network traffic.
distractors.B: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service - unrelated to network traffic filtering.
distractors.D: Amazon API Gateway manages and secures API endpoints - it doesn't provide subnet-level network ACLs.

explanation.concept: Multiple Regions provide redundancy against a Region-level failure
explanation.correct: Running web servers in multiple AWS Regions means the application can keep serving traffic even if an entire Region becomes unavailable, which increases availability.

distractors.A: Coupling refers to how tightly components depend on each other - deploying across Regions doesn't inherently increase coupling.
distractors.C: Multi-Region deployment can support security goals indirectly, but the property being directly increased here is availability, not security.
distractors.D: Durability is about long-term data preservation (e.g., S3's eleven 9s) - a separate concept from an application staying reachable.

explanation.concept: Pay-as-you-go turns fixed upfront spend into variable operational spend
explanation.correct: Pay-as-you-go pricing means customers pay only for what they use, without buying and owning hardware upfront - which reduces capital expenditures (CapEx) in favor of variable operational spend.

distractors.B: Pay-as-you-go is the opposite of paying upfront - it's a consumption-based model with no advance payment required.
distractors.C: Pay-as-you-go pricing applies across virtually all AWS services, not just EC2, S3, and RDS.
distractors.D: Pay-as-you-go shifts spending from capital to operational expenditure - it doesn't reduce operational expenditure, which is the ongoing cost of running the resources you consume.

explanation.concept: Physical security of the global infrastructure is entirely AWS's job
explanation.correct: AWS is responsible for the physical security of its data centers and global infrastructure - customers never have physical access to the hardware.

distractors.A: Lifecycle management of IAM credentials (creating, rotating, revoking) is the customer's responsibility.
distractors.C: Encrypting EBS volumes is a configuration choice the customer makes and manages.
distractors.D: Firewall configuration (e.g., security groups, network ACLs) is set up and maintained by the customer.

explanation.concept: Organizations centralizes accounts and billing under one management account
explanation.correct: AWS Organizations lets a company consolidate billing across multiple AWS accounts into a single payer account, combining usage for volume discounts and simplifying invoicing.

distractors.A: Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence and visualization tool - it doesn't perform account consolidation or billing.
distractors.C: AWS Budgets tracks spending against thresholds within an account or organization - it doesn't itself consolidate billing across accounts.
distractors.D: Amazon Forecast is a machine learning service for time-series forecasting - unrelated to billing consolidation.
